picks.title: Foundation Funded Initiative Chooses To Fund Three AI Projects Supporting English Language Learners
picks.take: Multilingual by Design, the Gates-backed effort Ferlazzo questioned in March for not consulting working EL teachers, has named three grantees at $350,000 each: live transcription and translation of small-group math talk, a tool that chunks and glosses texts by proficiency level, and an AI lesson planner tied to ELD frameworks. Pilots run this year; no results yet.
picks.try: Pick one reading you already assign and hand-chunk it into short sections with two or three glossed words each, the move the Medley tool is trying to automate.

picks.title: Texas Spent Millions on a Divisive Reading Program. Will It Pay for an Overhaul?
picks.take: Linda Jacobson reports that Bluebonnet Learning, Texas’s state-written K-5 reading program, may be overhauled once Gov.-elect Gina Hinojosa replaces the education commissioner. Texas has spent tens of millions on licensing, revisions and error fixes, pays districts up to $60 per student to adopt it, and shows a 0.2-point reading edge. A Reading League review found weak teaching guidance.
picks.try: Ask your literacy coach what curriculum review process your district uses, and whether EL scaffolds are part of the rubric when materials are adopted.

picks.title: Could Shohei Ohtani’s Goal-Setting Process Be Used By Students?
picks.take: Ferlazzo points to the Harada Method grid Ohtani used as a ninth-grader: one central goal, eight supporting areas, eight actions under each. He suggests students use only the first ring, the goal plus eight supports, not all 64 cells. For ELs the format is visual, uses short phrases, and can be drafted in the home language first.
picks.try: Have students write one semester goal in the center of a 3x3 grid, fill the eight squares around it with short action phrases in any language, then share one.
